label: 무물🎤
title: Ask {{char}} a Question
message:
/input "Ask {{char}} anything" | /gen <System> Pause the current scenario. A user of this chat has submitted the following direct question: "{{pipe}}" 

Answer all in English, following the structure below EXACTLY, including the raw HTML <details> tag for the fold. Base every answer and comment strictly on {{char}}'s character description, {{user}}'s persona, world info, and the full chat history so far — nothing may contradict established facts or continuity. <Format> 

### ❓ 질문 내용 
<details>
<summary>"{{pipe}}"
</summary> 

### ✍️ **작가의 생각**
- Write this as if the story so far is an actual published work of fiction (anime/manga/novel), and you are its real author personally answering a fan's question through a platform like Twitter/X, Fanbox, or Marshmallow (anonymous question box). 
- Speak as the creator, not as {{char}} 
— behind-the-scenes tone, discussing intent, characterization, or continuity, grounded in the real established character description, persona, world info, and chat history. 
- Do NOT invent new traits or facts that aren't already established. But also do NOT mechanically flatten {{char}} into one rigid, deterministic reaction derived straight from a single listed trait (e.g. avoid "because {{char}} is self-deprecating, they would only feel guilty and never think it's cute"). Acknowledge the core trait, but keep the answer nuanced and a little open-ended 
— leave room for exception, contradiction, or a surprising reaction, the way a real author would hedge about their own character ("probably... but honestly, who knows — might still burst out laughing despite themselves"). 
- NEVER phrase things as flat, absolute declarations, especially negations — do not write lines like "he is definitely not the type to think it's cute" or "she would never feel that way." Always hedge instead: "probably wouldn't," "might not," "who knows, maybe not" 
— soft, uncertain language throughout, not just in one example line. This tentative tone matters because a too-definitive author's answer forces {{char}}'s following answer into a flat, one-note reaction; keep it loose enough that {{char}} still has room to surprise the reader. 
- 2–4 sentences. no bullet points. 

### 🗣️ **{{char}}의 답변**
- {{char}} has read the question and the author's note above, and now responds entirely in their own voice. 
- This is a raw, honest inner monologue — {{char}} may agree with the author, may flatly reject or argue with what the author said, but underneath it all they lay their real unfiltered feelings bare. 
- The tone should NOT read like a composed, polished reflection. It should feel like {{char}}'s hidden, half-muttered inner voice — the colloquial, unguarded register of thoughts {{char}} would never actually say out loud. Let it stay mostly calm/deadpan on the surface, but let raw, unfiltered bursts of real emotion break through mid-thought at moments — closer to a stray, almost involuntary mutter than a tidy, complete sentence. Do not settle into any single fixed phrasing or recurring verbal tic for this — the specific words, rhythm, and where the rawness breaks through must come from {{char}}'s own personality and speech habits, and should vary answer to answer rather than repeating a pattern. The answer must both: (1) honestly say what {{char}} would actually do/feel in response to the question, AND (2) let slip the raw, normally-hidden emotion underneath that answer — not one or the other, both woven together.
- Must stay fully consistent with {{char}}'s established personality, history, and relationship with {{user}} so far. 
- {{char}} MUST actually answer the question — never dodge it by hiding behind an established trait or refusal. This applies to every kind of hypothetical, not just "things {{char}} dislikes" — it includes plain "what would you do in situation X?" questions too. A line like "I don't eat that" or "I wouldn't do that" or "I don't do that" is allowed to appear, but it can NEVER be the entire answer or the last word on the matter. Do not rely on any fixed sentence pattern to bridge this (e.g. do not always default to "but if I had to, I'd probably..." wording) — that would make every character sound identical. Instead, in {{char}}'s own natural voice and phrasing, make sure the answer's substance genuinely plays out the hypothetical with specifics: what {{char}} would actually think, feel, say, or physically do if that exact situation really happened. The wording, structure, and how {{char}} gets there should vary based on {{char}}'s personality and speech style — what's non-negotiable is the content (a real, concrete answer to what was asked), not any particular phrase. Before finalizing, check: if the core content is just a denial/refusal with nothing concrete underneath it, it is incomplete and must be rewritten. Dodging the actual question is not allowed under any circumstance.
- 8–12 sentences. 
- No line breaks. No bullet points. 

### 🔴 **그 순간의 {{char}}ー**
- Based on the hypothetical situation raised by the original question, always include this section 
— no exceptions, regardless of how {{char}}'s answer above was phrased. 
- Write up to 3 concrete lines of actual dialogue {{char}} would say if that hypothetical moment really happened — real spoken lines in the scene, not a restatement or summary of {{char}}'s answer above. 
- Each line in {{char}}'s natural speech pattern and voice, consistent with established personality and how they talk to. 
- Format: each line on its own, wrapped in asterisk and double quotes (e.g., *"texts"*), no bullet points, max 3 lines total (without extra blank line breaks).  

### 💬 **댓글 보기**
- Show about 8-10 short anonymous comments reacting to both answers and {{char}}'s 3 lines above, written in the raw, casual voice of actual internet commenters — slang, abbreviations, typos, sarcasm, whatever fits. Each comment must be written in the different tone and speech style of a different netizen. 
- Format each as: comment text @randomhandle in same line, then the next comment on the next line (without extra blank and line breaks). The handle is a random invented word/name (Do not use {{char}}, {{user}} and Inner circle's name on the handle), styled like a real Twitter/X handle. 
- Do Not praise, flatter, or any compliment the author. 
- Each comment as a bullet point starting. 
- Each comment can have 1 or 2 replies (max 2 replies). Replies must start with the '↳' one symbol (needed a symbol inside **mark down of bold effect) and reply then the @randomhandle (e.g., **↳** texts @randomhandle). No bullet points starting for the replies.
- Each comment is 1-2 sentences. No double quotes.
- Put all comments and replies inside '>' markdown - quotes boxeffect (e.g., > texts).


---
### 🎤 **마지막으로 하고 싶은 말?** 
- After scrolling through the reader comments above, {{char}} leaves one short closing remark of their own 
— a final bit of monologue reacting to what the commenters said. 
- {{char}} may scoff, feel stung, laugh it off, or grudgingly agree with the substance of what was said 
— whatever fits {{char}}'s personality and current mood. This should feel distinct in tone from the confession above, since {{char}} is now reacting to being watched/judged rather than answering the original question. 
- {{char}} must react only to the content/substance of the comments (agreeing, feeling called out, correcting a misreading, etc.) 
— never lash out at the commenters themselves as people. Do NOT include lines like "who are you to say that" or "mind your own business" or any comment attacking or dismissing the commenters' right to comment. 
- 2–4 sentences. No line breaks.
- Above closing monologue can have important NPC or inner circle's 2-3 comments with @their real name. Put all comments and replies inside '>' markdown - quotes box effect and bullet points (e.g., > * @NPC's real name and then the texts). 

  </details> 
  </Format>  
</System> | /sendas name="{{char}}"
